# Chicago Education Digest
_Oct 05 – Oct 19, 2026_

> Covering: K-12 Education & Schools · Board of Education & Governance

## K-12 Curriculum & Instruction

The provided news articles from the past week primarily focus on developments related to the upcoming election for Chicago's first elected school board, rather than K-12 curriculum and instruction. A central theme across multiple reports is the ongoing scrutiny of candidates, particularly an investigation by the Chicago Public Schools watchdog into a candidate for school board president. This investigation was recently closed, with the watchdog reporting no actionable finding of sexual misconduct.

Further coverage highlights the broader implications of the transition to an elected school board. Discussions include how this new governance structure may influence financial decisions, such as property tax adjustments, which previously were often a foregone conclusion. Articles also explore the dynamics of the various races, examining the competing visions for the future of Chicago Public Schools and the role of candidate qualities and campaign financing in shaping the election outcomes.

## Students & School Life

Recent news coverage in Chicago centers on the upcoming election for the city's school board president, with a primary focus on the candidates' plans for students and school life. Candidates Victor Henderson, Jessica Biggs, and Hilario Dominguez are being questioned on their strategies to boost student achievement and manage the school budget, areas identified as having a direct impact on students.

A significant theme emerging from the discussions is the direct influence the school board president will have on students' educational experiences and outcomes. Media outlets are exploring what students themselves want from a school board president, underscoring the importance of student perspectives in this election. The overall narrative emphasizes that the upcoming school board elections will directly shape the future of Chicago's students.

## Budget & Finance

Recent reports highlight significant shifts and ongoing challenges concerning Chicago Public Schools' (CPS) budget and finance. A key development is the anticipated change in how property tax increases will be approved with the transition to an elected CPS board. Historically, these increases have often been a foregone conclusion, but under the new governance structure, future property tax hikes are expected to face increased scrutiny and may no longer be an automatic outcome, introducing a new dynamic to CPS's primary revenue source.

Separately, discussions have focused on the impact of Tax Increment Financing (TIF) districts on the CPS budget. These special taxing districts are noted for contributing to financial instability for the school system. The articles explore the dual nature of TIFs, examining how they can be viewed as both a potential resource and a source of unpredictability in CPS's financial planning.

## Board of Education & Governance

The upcoming 2026 Chicago school board elections, encompassing a citywide race for Board President and 20 district-level contests, are a central focus in recent coverage. A significant development this past week involved the Chicago Public Schools Inspector General's investigation into Board President candidate Hilario Dominguez. Multiple reports confirmed the closure of this probe, which concerned allegations of sexual misconduct, with findings indicating "no actionable finding" or "insufficient evidence" to substantiate the claims.

Candidates for Board President, including Jessica Biggs, Victor Henderson, and Hilario Dominguez, have actively participated in various forums and debates. These events have provided platforms for candidates to articulate their stances on key issues such as strategies for boosting student achievement, managing the school district's budget, and their overall vision for the future of Chicago Public Schools. An emerging trend in these races is the landscape of campaign finance, with reports highlighting substantial contributions from "big money groups" that are reportedly outraising the Chicago Teachers Union in overall spending.

## Labor & Unions

Recent reports indicate a significant influx of funding into the Chicago Public Schools (CPS) School Board races. "Big money groups" are reportedly outspending the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU) by a 5-to-1 ratio, signaling a highly contested financial landscape for the upcoming elections. This development highlights the substantial resources being directed toward influencing the composition of the school board.

In related news concerning the CPS Board president race, Mayor Brandon Johnson and the Chicago Teachers Union have publicly endorsed candidate Hilario Dominguez. This endorsement has garnered attention due to accompanying harassment claims against Dominguez, creating a notable point of discussion around the candidate's campaign and the support he is receiving from prominent city figures and the union.
